units.description: unit of specific thermal resistance according to the Imperial system of units

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit Hour per British Thermal Unit (international Definition)
units.description:
$\textit{Degree Fahrenheit Hour per BTU}$ is an Imperial unit for 'Thermal Resistance' expressed as
    $degF-h/Btu$.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit Hour per British Thermal Unit (thermochemical Definition)
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Degree Fahrenheit hour per British thermal unit (thermochemical)}$ is a non SI-conform
    unit of the thermal resistance according to the Imperial system of units.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit per Bar
units.description:
$\textit{Degree Fahrenheit per bar}$ is the traditional unit degree Fahrenheit for temperature according
    to the Anglo-American system of units divided by the unit bar.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit per Hour
units.description: $\textit{Degree Fahrenheit per Hour}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Time' expressed as $degF / h$.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit per Kelvin
units.description:
traditional unit degree Fahrenheit for temperature according to the Anglo-American system of units
    divided by the SI base unit Kelvin

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit per Minute
units.description: $\textit{Degree Fahrenheit per Minute}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Time' expressed as $degF / m$.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit per Second
units.description: $\textit{Degree Fahrenheit per Second}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Time' expressed as $degF / s$.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit per Square Second
units.description:
'Degree Fahrenheit per Square Second' is a unit for expressing the acceleration of a temperature
    expressed as 'degF /s2'.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit Second per British Thermal Unit (international Definition)
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Degree Fahrenheit Second per British thermal unit (international table)}$ is a non SI-conform unit
   of the thermal resistance according to the Imperial system of units.

units.label: Degree Fahrenheit Second per British Thermal Unit (thermochemical Definition)
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Degree Fahrenheit Second per British thermal unit (thermochemical)}$ is a non SI-conform unit
   of the thermal resistance according to the Imperial system of units.

units.label: Degree Rankine
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Degree Rankine}$ is a thermodynamic (absolute) temperature scale.
  The symbol for degrees Rankine is $^\circ R$ or $^\circ Ra$ if necessary to distinguish it from the Rømer and Réaumur scales).
  Zero on both the Kelvin and Rankine scales is absolute zero, but the Rankine degree is defined as equal
   to one degree Fahrenheit, rather than the one degree Celsius used by the Kelvin scale.
  A temperature of $-459.67 ^\circ F$ is exactly equal to $0 ^\circ R$.

units.label: Degree Rankine per Hour
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Degree Rankine per Hour}$ is a rate of change of temperature measured in degree
    Rankine in periods of one hour.

units.label: Degree Rankine per Minute
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Degree Rankine per Minute}$ is a rate of change of temperature measured in degree
    Rankine in periods of one minute.

units.label: Degree Rankine per Second
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Degree Rankine per Second}$ is a rate of change of temperature measured in degree
    Rankine in periods of one second.

units.label: Denier
units.description:
Denier or den is a unit of measure for the linear mass density of fibers. It is defined as the mass in
    grams per 9,000 meters. In the International System of Units the tex is used instead (see below). The denier is based on a
    natural standard: a single strand of silk is approximately one denier. A 9,000-meter strand of silk weighs about one gram. The
    term denier is from the French denier, a coin of small value (worth 1/12 of a sou). Applied to yarn, a denier was held to be
    equal in weight to 1/24 of an ounce. The term microdenier is used to describe filaments that weigh less than one gram per
    9,000 meter length.

units.label: Diopter
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Dioptre}$, or $\textit{Diopter}$, is a unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens or curved mirror,
   which is equal to the reciprocal of the focal length measured in metres (that is, $1/metre$).
  For example, a $3 \; dioptre$ lens brings parallel rays of light to focus at $1/3\,metre$.
  The same unit is also sometimes used for other reciprocals of distance, particularly radii of curvature
   and the vergence of optical beams.
  Though the diopter is based on the SI-metric system it has not been included in the standard so that there is
   no international name or abbreviation for this unit of measurement within the international system of units
    this unit for optical power would need to be specified explicitly as the inverse metre.

units.label: Dots per Inch
units.description:
point density as amount of the picture base element divided by the unit inch according to the
    Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units

units.label: Dram (UK)
units.description:
non SI-conforming unit of mass comes from the Anglo-American Troy or Apothecaries' Weight System of
    units which is  mainly used in England, in the Netherlands and in the USA as a commercial weight

units.label: Dram (US)
units.description:
non SI-conform unit of the mass according to the avoirdupois system of units: 1 dram (av. ) = 1/16
    ounce (av. ) = 1/256 pound (av.)

units.label: Dobson Unit
units.description:
The Dobson unit (DU) is a unit of measurement of the amount of a trace gas in a vertical column through
    the Earth's atmosphere at standard conditions (STP).

units.label: Penny Weight
units.description: "Penny Weight" is a unit for  'Mass' expressed as $dwt$.

units.label: Dyne
units.description:
In physics, the $dyne$ is a unit of force specified in the centimetre-gram-second (CGS) system of units.
    The $dyne$ is a unit of force specified in the centimetre-gram-second (CGS) system of units. One $dyne$ is equal to
    $\SI{10}{\micro\newton}$. Equivalently, the $dyne$ is defined as 'the force required to accelerate a mass of one gram at a
    rate of one centimetre per square second'. A $\textit{dyne per centimetre}$ is the unit traditionally used to measure surface
    tension.

units.label: Dyne Centimetre
units.description: "Dyne Centimeter" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Torque' expressed as $dyn-cm$.

units.label: Dyne Metre
units.description: [CGS] unit of the rotational moment

units.label: Dyne per Centimetre
units.description: CGS unit of the surface tension

units.label: Dyne per Square Centimetre
units.description: "Dyne per Square Centimeter" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Force Per Area' expressed as $dyn/cm^{2}$.

units.label: Dyne Second per Centimetre
units.description: CGS unit of the mechanical impedance

units.label: Dyne Second per Cubic Centimetre
units.description: CGS unit of the acoustic image impedance of the medium

units.label: Dyne Second per Quintic Centimetre
units.description: [CGS] unit of the acoustic impedance (volume flow rate-related pressure)

units.label: Dalton
units.description:
The unified atomic mass unit (symbol: $\mu$) or dalton (symbol: Da) is a unit that is used for
    indicating mass on an atomic or molecular scale. It is defined as one twelfth of the rest mass of an unbound atom of carbon-12
    in its nuclear and electronic ground state, and has a value of $1.660538782(83) \times 10^{-27} kg$. One $Da$ is
    approximately equal to the mass of one proton or one neutron. The CIPM have categorised it as a "non-SI unit whose values in
    SI units must be obtained experimentally".

units.label: Debye
units.description: "Debye" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Electric Dipole Moment' expressed as $D$.

units.label: Decaare
units.description: unit of the area which is mainly common in the agriculture and forestry: 1 da = 10 a

units.label: Decacoulomb
units.description: A DecaCoulomb is $10 C$.

units.label: Decagram
units.description: 0.01-fold of the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Decalitre
units.description: 10-fold of the unit litre

units.label: Decametre
units.description: 10-fold of the SI base unit metre

units.label: Cubic Decametre
units.description: 1 000-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre by exponent 3

units.label: Decapascal
units.description: 10-fold of the derived SI unit pascal

units.label: Decapoise
units.description: 10-fold of the CGS unit of the dynamic viscosity poise

units.label: Decibel
units.description:
A customary logarithmic measure most commonly used (in various ways) for measuring sound.Sound is
    measured on a logarithmic scale. Informally, if one sound is $1\,bel$ (10 decibels) "louder" than another, this means the
    louder sound is 10 times louder than the fainter one. A difference of 20 decibels corresponds to an increase of 10 x 10 or 100
    times in intensity. The beginning of the scale, 0 decibels, can be set in different ways, depending on exactly the aspect of
    sound being measured. For sound intensity (the power of the sound waves per unit of area) $0\,decibel$ is equal to
    $1\,picoWatts\,per\,Metre\,Squared$. This corresponds approximately to the faintest sound that can be detected by a person
    who has good hearing. For sound pressure (the pressure exerted by the sound waves) 0 decibels equals
    $20\,micropascals\,RMS$, and for sound power $0\,decibels$ sometimes equals $1\,picoWatt$. In all cases, one decibel
    equals $\approx\,0.115129\,neper$.

units.label: Decibel Milliwatt
units.description:
unit of level used to indicate that a power ratio is expressed in decibel (dB) with reference to one
    milliwatt (mW)

units.label: Decibel Milliwatt per Megahertz
units.description:
unit of level used to indicate that a power ratio is expressed in decibel (dB) with reference to one
    milliwatt (mW) devided by the 1,000,000-fold of the derived unit hertz

units.label: Decibel per Kilometre
units.description: 0.1-fold of the unit bel divided by 1,000-fold of the SI base unit metre

units.label: Decibel per Metre
units.description: 0.1-fold of the unit bel divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Decibel Watt
units.description:
The decibel watt or dBW is a unit for the measurement of the strength of a signal expressed in decibels
    relative to one watt.

units.label: Decibar
units.description:
The bar is a non-SI unit of pressure, defined by the IUPAC as exactly equal to 100,000 Pa. It is about
    equal to the atmospheric pressure on Earth at sea level, and since 1982 the IUPAC has recommended that the standard for
    atmospheric pressure should be harmonized to $100,000 Pa = 1 bar \approx 750.0616827 Torr$. Units derived from the bar are
    the megabar (symbol: Mbar), kilobar (symbol: kbar), decibar (symbol: dbar), centibar (symbol: cbar), and millibar (symbol:
    mbar or mb). They are not SI or cgs units, but they are accepted for use with the SI.

units.label: Decibar per Year
units.description:
A rate of change of pressure expressed in decibars over a period of an average calendar year (365.25
    days).

units.label: Decibel with A-weighting
units.description: Logarithmic unit of sound pressure level with frequency weighting A

units.label: Decibel Carrier Unit
units.description: "Decibel Carrier Unit" is a logarithmic unit for  'Signal Detection Threshold' expressed as $dBc$.

units.label: Decibel Isotropic
units.description: Logarithmic antenna gain of a transmitted or received signal

units.label: Decibel Referred to 1mw
units.description: "Decibel Referred to 1mw" is a 'Logarithmic Dimensionless Ratio' expressed as $dBm$.

units.label: Decibel with Z-weighting
units.description: Logarithmic unit of sound pressure level with frequency weighting Z (ZERO or linear weighting)

units.label: Decicoulomb
units.description: A DeciCoulomb is $10^{-1} C$.

units.label: Decigram
units.description: 0.0001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Decilitre
units.description: 0.1-fold of the unit litre

units.label: Decilitre per Gram
units.description: 0.1-fold of the unit of the volume litre divided by the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Decimetre
units.description: A decimeter is a tenth of a meter.

units.label: Square Decimetre
units.description: 0.1-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 2

units.label: Cubic Decimetre
units.description: 0.1-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3

units.label: Cubic Decimetre per Day
units.description:
0,001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 divided by the unit for time
    day

units.label: Cubic Decimetre per Hour
units.description: 0,001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 divided by the unit hour

units.label: Cubic Decimetre per Kilogram
units.description: 0.001-fold of the power of the SI base unit meter by exponent 3 divided by the SI based unit kilogramm

units.label: Cubic Decimetre per Cubic Metre
units.description:
volume ratio consisting of the 0.001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent
    3 divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3

units.label: Cubic Decimetre per Minute
units.description:
0,001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 divided by the unit for time
    minute

units.label: Cubic Decimetre per Mole
units.description:
0,001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 divided by the SI base unit
    mol

units.label: Cubic Decimetre per Second
units.description:
0,001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 divided by the unit for time
    second

units.label: Decinewton Metre
units.description: 0.1-fold of the product of the derived SI unit joule and the SI base unit metre

units.label: Decisiemens per Metre
units.description: Decisiemens per metre.

units.label: Decisecond
units.description: "Decisecond" is an SI unit for 'Time' expressed as $ds$.

units.label: Deci Metric Ton
units.description: 100-fold of the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Denier
units.description:
Denier or den is a unit of measure for the linear mass density of fibers. It is defined as the mass in
    grams per 9,000 meters. In the International System of Units the tex is used instead (see below). The denier is based on a
    natural standard: a single strand of silk is approximately one denier. A 9,000-meter strand of silk weighs about one gram. The
    term denier is from the French denier, a coin of small value (worth 1/12 of a sou). Applied to yarn, a denier was held to be
    equal in weight to 1/24 of an ounce. The term microdenier is used to describe filaments that weigh less than one gram per
    9,000 meter length.

units.label: Elementary Charge
units.description:
$\textit{Elementary Charge}$, usually denoted as $e$, is the electric charge carried by a single proton,
  or equivalently, the negation (opposite) of the electric charge carried by a single electron.
  This elementary charge is a fundamental physical constant.
  To avoid confusion over its sign, e is sometimes called the elementary positive charge.
  This charge has a measured value of approximately $1.602176634 \times 10^{-19} coulombs$.
  In the cgs system, $e$ is $4.80320471257026372 \times 10^{-10} statcoulombs$.

units.label: Enzyme Unit
units.description: unit to express the catalytic activity of a specified chemical reaction

units.label: Enzyme Unit per Litre
units.description: amount of enzyme units divided by litre

units.label: Equivalent
units.description:
An equivalent is an amount of substance defined by the number of unit charges, positive or
    negative, that the relevant reactive species donate, accept, or exchange in a chemical process. It expresses stoichiometric
    charge capacity rather than the number of particles of a substance.

units.label: Equivalent per Litre
units.description: Equivalent per litre is a unit of equivalent concentration expressing the amount of an ionic substance in equivalents per litre of solution.

units.label: Erg
units.description:
An erg is the unit of energy and mechanical work in the centimetre-gram-second (CGS) system of units,
    symbol 'erg'. Its name is derived from the Greek ergon, meaning 'work'. An erg is the amount of work done by a force of one
    dyne exerted for a distance of one centimeter. In the CGS base units, it is equal to one gram centimeter-squared per
    second-squared ($g \cdot cm^2/s^2$). It is thus equal to $10^{-7}$ joules or 100 nanojoules in SI units. $1 erg = 10^{-7} J =
    100 nJ$,  $1 erg = 624.15 GeV = 6.2415 \times 10^{11} eV$, $1 erg = 1 dyne\cdot cm = 1 g \cdot cm^2/s^2$.

units.label: Erg Square Centimetre
units.description: [CGS] unit of the atomic stopping power

units.label: Erg Square Centimetre per Gram
units.description: [CGS] unit of the mass stopping power

units.label: Erg per Centimetre
units.description: CGS unit of the length-related energy

units.label: Erg per Square Centimetre
units.description:
Derived CGS unit erg divided by the 0.0001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre by exponent
    2

units.label: Erg per Square Centimetre Second
units.description:
"Erg per Square Centimeter Second" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Power Per Area' expressed as
    $erg/(cm^{2}-s)$.

units.label: Erg per Gram
units.description: CGS unit of the mass-related energy

units.label: Erg per Gram Second
units.description: CGS unit of the mass-related power

units.label: Erg per Second
units.description: "Erg per Second" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Power' expressed as $erg/s$.

units.label: Erlang
units.description:
The "Erlang" is a dimensionless unit that is used in telephony as a measure of offered load or carried
    load on service-providing elements such as telephone circuits or telephone switching equipment.

units.label: Electron Volt
units.description:
An electron volt (eV) is the energy that an electron gains when it travels through a potential of one
    volt. You can imagine that the electron starts at the negative plate of a parallel plate capacitor and accelerates to the
    positive plate, which is at one volt higher potential. Numerically $1 eV$ approximates $1.6x10^{-19} joules$, where $1 joule$
    is $6.2x10^{18} eV$. For example, it would take $6.2x10^{20} eV/sec$ to light a 100 watt light bulb.

units.label: Electron Volt Square Metre
units.description: product of the unit electronvolt and the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 2

units.label: Electron Volt Square Metre per Kilogram
units.description:
product of the unit electronvolt and the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 2 divided by
    the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Electron Volt per Angstrom
units.description: unit electronvolt divided by the unit angstrom

units.label: Electron Volt per Kelvin
units.description: $\textit{Electron Volt per Kelvin}$ is a unit for 'Heat Capacity' expressed as $ev/K$.

units.label: Electron Volt per Metre
units.description: unit electronvolt divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Electron Volt per Tesla
units.description: The unit $\textit{Electron Volt per Tesla}$ is a unit for $\textit{Magnetic Dipole Moment}$ expressed as $eV T^{-1}$.

units.label: Electron Volt Second
units.description: "Electron Volt Second" is a unit for  'Angular Momentum' expressed as $eV s$.

units.label: Hartree
units.description:
The $\textit{Hartree}$ (symbol: $E_h$ or $Ha$), also known as the $\text{Hartree\,Energy}$, is the atomic unit of energy. The hartree energy is equal to the absolute value of the electric potential energy of the hydrogen atom in its ground state. The energy of the electron in an H-atom in its ground state is $-E_H$, where $E_H= 2 R_\infty \cdot hc_0$. The 2006 CODATA recommended value was $E_H = 4.35974394(22) \times 10^{-18} J = 27.21138386(68) eV$.

Definition:
$E_H= \frac{e^2}{4\pi \epsilon_0 a_0 }$
where, $e$ is the elementary charge, $\epsilon_0$ is the electric constant, and $a_0$ is the Bohr radius.'

units.label: Earth Mass
units.description:
Earth mass ($M_{\oplus}$) is the unit of mass equal to that of the Earth. In SI Units, $1 M_{\oplus} =
    5.9722 \times 10^{24} kg$. Earth mass is often used to describe masses of rocky terrestrial planets. The four terrestrial
    planets of the Solar System, Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars, have masses of 0.055, 0.815, 1.000, and 0.107 Earth masses
    respectively.

units.label: Elementary Charge
units.description:
$\textit{Elementary Charge}$, usually denoted as $e$, is the electric charge carried by a single proton,
    or equivalently, the negation (opposite) of the electric charge carried by a single electron. This elementary charge is a
    fundamental physical constant. To avoid confusion over its sign, e is sometimes called the elementary positive charge. This
    charge has a measured value of approximately $1.602176634 \times 10^{-19} coulombs$. In the cgs system, $e$ is
    $4.80320471257026372 \times 10^{-10} statcoulombs$.

units.label: Exabit per Second
units.description: 1,000,000,000,000,000,000-fold of the unit bit divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Exabyte
units.description:
The exabyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information. The prefix exa means 10^18 in the
    International System of Units (SI), so ExaByte is 10^18 Bytes.

units.label: Exacoulomb
units.description: An ExaCoulomb is $10^{18} C$.

units.label: Exajoule
units.description: 1,000,000,000,000,000,000-fold of the derived SI unit joule

units.label: Exajoule per Second
units.description: 1,000,000,000,000,000,000-fold of the SI derived unit joule divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Exavolt Ampere
units.description: 1,000,000,000,000,000,000-fold of the product of the SI base unit volt with the SI base unit ampere

units.label: Exa Volt Ampere
units.description: 1,000,000,000,000,000,000-fold of the product of the SI base unit volt with the SI base unit ampere

units.label: Exbibit per Metre
units.description: 1,152,921,504,606,846,976-fold of the unit bit divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Exbibit per Square Metre
units.description:
1,152,921,504,606,846,976-fold of the unit bit divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 2

units.label: Exbibit per Cubic Metre
units.description:
1,152,921,504,606,846,976-fold of the unit bit divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3

units.label: Exbibyte
units.description: The exbibyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information. The prefix exbi means 1024^6

units.label: Faraday
units.description: "Faraday" is a unit for  'Electric Charge' expressed as $F$.

units.label: Fractional Area
units.description: "Fractional area" is a unit for  'Solid Angle' expressed as $fa$.

units.label: Farad
units.description:
The SI unit of electric capacitance. Very early in the study of electricity scientists discovered that a
    pair of conductors separated by an insulator can store a much larger charge than an isolated conductor can store. The better
    the insulator, the larger the charge that the conductors can hold. This property of a circuit is called capacitance, and it is
    measured in farads. One farad is defined as the ability to store one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference
    between the two conductors. This is a natural definition, but the unit it defines is very large. In practical circuits,
    capacitance is often measured in microfarads, nanofarads, or sometimes even in picofarads (10-12 farad, or trillionths of a
    farad). The unit is named for the British physicist Michael Faraday (1791-1867), who was known for his work in electricity and
    electrochemistry.

units.label: Farad per Kilometre
units.description: SI derived unit farad divided by the 1 000-fold of the SI base unit metre

units.label: Farad per Metre
units.description:
Farad Per Meter ($F/m$) is a unit in the category of Electric permittivity. It is also known as
    farad/meter. This unit is commonly used in the SI unit system. Farad Per Meter has a dimension of M-1L-3T4I2 where $M$ is
    mass, $L$ is length, $T$ is time, and $I$ is electric current. This unit is the standard SI unit in this category.

units.label: Abfarad
units.description:
An abfarad is an obsolete electromagnetic (CGS) unit of capacitance equal to $10^{9}$ farads
    (1,000,000,000 F or 1 GF). The absolute farad of the e.m.u. system, for a steady current identically $abC/abV$, and
    identically reciprocal abdaraf. 1 abF = 1 GF.

units.label: Abfarad per Centimetre
units.description:
The absolute dielectric constant of free space is defined as the ratio of displacement to the electric
    field intensity. The unit of measure is the abfarad per centimeter, a derived CGS unit.

units.label: Statfarad
units.description:
The $\text{Statfarad (statF)}$ is a unit in the category of Electric capacitance.
  It is also known as $statfarads$.
  This unit is commonly used in the cgs unit system.
  $Statfarad$ has a dimension of $M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4I^2$ where $M$ is mass, $L$ is length, $T$ is time, and $I$ is electric current.
  It can be converted to the corresponding standard SI unit F by multiplying its value by a factor of 1.11265E-012.

units.label: Fathom
units.description:
A fathom = 1.8288 meters, is a unit of length in the imperial and the U.S. customary systems, used
    especially for measuring the depth of water. There are two yards in an imperial or U.S. fathom. Originally based on the
    distance between the man's outstretched arms, the size of a fathom has varied slightly depending on whether it was defined as
    a thousandth of an (Admiralty) nautical mile or as a multiple of the imperial yard.  Abbreviations: f, fath, fm, fth, fthm.

units.label: Board Foot
units.description:
The board-foot is a specialized unit of measure for the volume of lumber in the United States and Canada.
    It is the volume of a one-foot length of a board one foot wide and one inch thick. Board-foot can be abbreviated FBM (for
    'foot, board measure'), BDFT, or BF. Thousand board-feet can be abbreviated as MFBM, MBFT or MBF.

units.label: Foot Candle
units.description: "Foot Candle" is a unit for  'Luminous Flux Per Area' expressed as $fc$.

units.label: Floating Point Operations per Second
units.description: Floating point operations divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Fermi
units.description:
The $\textit{fermi}$, or $\textit{femtometer}$ (other spelling $femtometre$, symbol $fm$) is an SI unit
    of length equal to $10^{-15} metre$. This distance is often encountered in nuclear physics as a characteristic of this scale.
    The symbol for the fermi is also $fm$.

units.label: Franklin
units.description: "Franklin" is a unit for  'Electric Charge' expressed as $Fr$.

units.label: Fraction
units.description: Fraction is a unit for 'Dimensionless Ratio' expressed as the value of the ratio itself.

units.label: Frame per Second
units.description: "Frame per Second" is a unit for  'Video Frame Rate' expressed as $fps$.

units.label: Foot
units.description:
A foot is a unit of length defined as being 0.3048 m exactly and used in the imperial system of units and
    United States customary units. It is subdivided into 12 inches. The foot is still officially used in Canada and still commonly
    used in the United Kingdom, although the latter has partially metricated its units of measurement.

units.label: Foot Hour per Gallon (UK)
units.description:
quotient of the unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per unit
    gallon (UK) according to the Anglo-American system of units and unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the
    avoirdupois system of units per product of foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units and unit of
    time hour

units.label: Foot Hour per Us Gallon
units.description:
quotient of the unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per unit
    gallon (US) according to the Anglo-American system of units and unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the
    avoirdupois system of units per product of foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units and unit of
    time hour

units.label: Foot Hour per Cubic Inch
units.description:
quotient of the unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per power
    of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the exponent 3 and unit of the mass
    avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per product of foot according to the Anglo-American and the
    Imperial system of units and unit of time hour

units.label: Foot Pound Force
units.description:
"Foot Pound Force" is an Imperial unit for torque or moment of force expressed as $ft-lbf$. It has been deprecated
    in favor of two more precise units: unit:FT-LB_F_Torque and unit:FT-LB_F_Energy of distinct extended dimensionality.

units.label: Foot Pound Force per Square Foot
units.description: "Foot Pound per Square Foot" is an Imperial unit for  'Energy Per Area' expressed as $ft-lbf/ft^{2}$.

units.label: Foot Pound Force per Square Foot Second
units.description:
"Foot Pound Force per Square Foot Second" is an Imperial unit for  'Power Per Area' expressed as $ft
    \cdot lbf/(ft^2 \cdot s)$.

units.label: Foot Pound Force per Hour
units.description: "Foot Pound Force per Hour" is an Imperial unit for  'Power' expressed as $ft-lbf/h$.

units.label: Foot Pound Force per Square Metre
units.description: "Foot Pound Force per Square Meter" is a unit for  'Energy Per Area' expressed as $ft-lbf/m^{2}$.

units.label: Foot Pound Force per Minute
units.description: "Foot Pound Force per Minute" is an Imperial unit for  'Power' expressed as $ft-lbf/min$.

units.label: Foot Pound Force per Second
units.description: "Foot Pound Force per Second" is an Imperial unit for  'Power' expressed as $ft-lbf/s$.

units.label: Foot Pound Force Second
units.description: "Foot Pound Force Second" is a unit for  'Angular Momentum' expressed as $lbf / s$.

units.label: Foot Pound Force (Energy)
units.description: "Foot Pound Force" is an Imperial unit for energy expressed as $ft-lbf$. It is the energy transferred upon applying a force of one pound-force (LB_F) through a linear displacement of one foot (FT).

units.label: Foot Pound Force (Torque)
units.description: "Foot Pound Force" is an Imperial unit for torque or moment of force expressed as $ft-lbf$.

units.label: Foot Poundal
units.description: "Foot Poundal" is an Imperial unit for  'Energy And Work' expressed as $ft-pdl$.

units.label: Foot per Day
units.description: "Foot per Day" is an Imperial unit for  'Linear Velocity' expressed as $ft/d$.

units.label: Foot per Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
unit foot as a linear measure according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units
    divided by the unit for temperature degree Fahrenheit

units.label: Foot per Hour
units.description: "Foot per Hour" is an Imperial unit for  'Linear Velocity' expressed as $ft/h$.

units.label: Foot per Minute
units.description: "Foot per Minute" is an Imperial unit for  'Linear Velocity' expressed as $ft/min$.

units.label: Foot per Psi
units.description:
unit foot as a linear measure according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units divided by
    the composed unit for pressure (pound-force square inch)

units.label: Foot per Second
units.description:
$\textit{foot per second}$ (plural $\textit{feet per second}$) is a unit of both speed (scalar) and
    velocity (vector quantity, which includes direction). It expresses the distance in feet ($ft$) traveled or displaced, divided
    by the time in seconds ($s$, or $sec$). The corresponding unit in the International System of Units (SI) is the
    $\textit{metre per second}$. Abbreviations include $ft/s$, $ft/sec$ and $fps$, and the rarely used scientific notation
    $ft\,s$.

units.label: Foot per Second Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
unit foot as a linear measure according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units divided by
    the product of the SI base unit second and the traditional unit degree Fahrenheit

units.label: Foot per Second Psi
units.description:
quotient of the unit foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units and the SI
    base unit second divided by the composed unit for pressure (pound-force per square inch)

units.label: Foot per Square Second
units.description:
$\textit{Foot per Square Second}$ is an Imperial unit for $\textit{Linear Acceleration}$ expressed as
    $ft/s^2$.

units.label: Foot Second per Gallon (UK)
units.description:
quotient of the unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per unit
    gallon (UK) according to the Anglo-American system of units and unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the
    avoirdupois system of units per product of foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units and SI base
    unit second

units.label: Foot Second per Us Gallon
units.description:
quotient of the unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per unit
    gallon (US) according to the Anglo-American system of units and unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the
    avoirdupois system of units per product of foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units and SI base
    unit second

units.label: Foot Second per Cubic Inch
units.description:
quotient of the unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per power
    of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the exponent 3 and unit of the mass
    avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per product of foot according to the Anglo-American and the
    Imperial system of units and SI base unit second

units.label: Square Foot
units.description:
The square foot (plural square feet; abbreviated $ft^2$ or $sq \, ft$) is an imperial unit and U.S.
    customary unit of area, used mainly in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Hong Kong, Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and
    Afghanistan. It is defined as the area of a square with sides of 1 foot in length.

units.label: Square Foot Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
$\textit{Square Foot Degree Fahrenheit}$ is an Imperial unit for 'Area Temperature' expressed as
    $ft^{2}-degF$.

units.label: Square Foot Hour Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
$\textit{Square Foot Hour Degree Fahrenheit}$ is an Imperial unit for 'Area Time Temperature' expressed
    as $ft^{2}-h-degF$.

units.label: Square Foot Hour Degree Fahrenheit per British Thermal Unit (international Definition)
units.description:
$\textit{Square Foot Hour Degree Fahrenheit per BTU}$ is an Imperial unit for 'Thermal Insulance'
    expressed as $(degF-h-ft^{2})/Btu$.

units.label: Square Foot per British Thermal Unit (international Definition) Inch
Square Foot per Hour
units.description:
$\textit{Square Foot per Hour}$ is an Imperial unit for $\textit{Kinematic Viscosity}$ and
    $\textit{Thermal Diffusivity}$ expressed as $ft^{2}/hr$.

units.label: Square Foot per Second
units.description: "Square Foot per Second" is an Imperial unit for  'Kinematic Viscosity' expressed as $ft^{2}/s$.

units.label: Square Foot Second Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
$\textit{Square Foot Second Degree Fahrenheit}$ is an Imperial unit for 'Area Time Temperature'
    expressed as $ft^{2}\cdot s\cdot degF$.

units.label: Cubic Foot
units.description:
The cubic foot is an Imperial and US customary unit of volume, used in the United States and the United Kingdom.
  It is defined as the volume of a cube with sides of one foot (0.3048 m) in length.
  To calculate cubic feet multiply length X width X height.

units.label: Cubic Foot per Day
units.description:
power of the unit foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the
    exponent 3 divided by the unit for time day

units.label: Cubic Foot per Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
power of the unit foot as a linear measure according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system
    of units with the exponent 3 divided by the unit for temperature degree Fahrenheit

units.label: Cubic Foot per Hour
units.description:
power of the unit foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the
    exponent 3 divided by the unit hour

units.label: Cubic Foot per Pound Mass
units.description:
power of the unit foot according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system of units by exponent 3 divided
    by the unit avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois unit system

units.label: Cubic Foot per Minute
units.description: "Cubic Foot per Minute" is an Imperial unit for  'Volume Per Unit Time' expressed as $ft^3/min$.

units.label: Cubic Foot per Minute Square Foot
units.description:
unit of the volume flow rate according to the Anglio-American and imperial system of units cubic
    foot per minute related to the transfer area according to the Anglian American and Imperial system of units square foot

units.label: Cubic Foot per Psi
units.description:
power of the unit foot as a linear measure according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of
    units with the exponent 3 divided by the composed unit for pressure (pound-force per square inch)

units.label: Cubic Foot per Second
units.description: "Cubic Foot per Second" is an Imperial unit for $ \textit{Volume Per Unit Time}$ expressed as $ft^3/s$.

units.label: Quartic Foot
units.description: power of the unit foot according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system of units by exponent 4

units.label: Foot of Water
units.description: "Foot of Water" is a unit for  'Force Per Area' expressed as $ftH2O$.

units.label: Foot of Water (39.2 °F)
units.description:
non SI-conforming unit of pressure according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system for units, whereas
    the value of 1 ftH₂O is equivalent to the static pressure generated by a head of water at a temperature 39.2°F with a height
    of 1 foot

units.label: Foot of Mercury
units.description:
A non-SI-conforming unit of pressure, at which 1 ftHg corresponds to the static pressure, which is
    excited by a mercury column with a height of 1 foot

units.label: Us Survey Foot
units.description: The U.S. Survey Foot was officially deprecated on December 31, 2022. For more information see Federal Register (October 5, 2020, 85 FR 62698, p. 62698)

units.label: Furlong
units.description:
A furlong is a measure of distance in imperial units and U.S. customary units equal to one-eighth of a
    mile, equivalent to 220 yards, 660 feet, 40 rods, or 10 chains. The exact value of the furlong varies slightly among
    English-speaking countries. Five furlongs are approximately 1 kilometre (1.0058 km is a closer approximation). Since the
    original definition of the metre was one-quarter of one ten-millionth of the circumference of the Earth (along the great
    circle coincident with the meridian of longitude passing through Paris), the circumference of the Earth is about 40,000 km or
    about 200,000 furlongs.

units.label: Femtoampere
units.description: 0.000000000000001-fold of the unit ampere

units.label: Femtocoulomb
units.description: A FemtoCoulomb is $10^{-15} C$.

units.label: Femtofarad
units.description: 0.000000000000001-fold of the unit farad

units.label: Femtogram
units.description: 0.000000000000001-fold of the unit gram

units.label: Femtogram per Kilogram
units.description: One part per 10**18 by mass of the measurand in the matrix.

units.label: Femtogram per Litre
units.description: One 10**18 part of the SI standard unit of mass of the measurand per litre volume of matrix..

units.label: Femtojoule
units.description: 0.000000000000001-fold of the derived SI unit joule

units.label: Femtolitre
units.description: 0.000000000000001-fold of the unit litre

units.label: Femtometre
units.description:
The $\textit{femtometre}$ is an SI unit of length equal to $10^{-15} meter$. This distance can also be
    called $\textit{fermi}$ and was so named in honour of Enrico Fermi. It is often encountered in nuclear physics as a
    characteristic of this scale. The symbol for the fermi is also $fm$.

units.label: Femtomole per Kilogram
units.description: A 10**15 part quantity of substance of the measurand per kilogram mass of matrix.

units.label: Femtomole per Litre
units.description: A 10**18 part quantity of substance of the measurand per litre volume of matrix.

units.label: Femtosecond
units.description: 0.000000000000001-fold of the SI base unit second

units.label: Femtovolt
units.description: 0.000000000000001-fold of the SI derived unit volt

units.label: Gravity
units.description: "Gravity" is a unit for  'Linear Acceleration' expressed as $G$.

units.label: Galileo
units.description: CGS unit of acceleration called gal with the definition: 1 Gal = 1 cm/s

units.label: Imperial Gallon
units.description: A British gallon used in liquid and dry measurement approximately 1.2 U.S. gallons, or 4.54 liters

units.label: Gallon (UK)
units.description: unit of the volume for fluids according to the Imperial system of units

units.label: Gallon (UK) per Day
units.description: unit gallon (UK dry or liq.) according to the Imperial system of units divided by the SI unit day

units.label: Gallon (UK) per Hour
units.description: unit gallon (UK dry or Liq.) according to the Imperial system of units divided by the SI unit hour

units.label: Gallon (UK) per Minute
units.description:
unit gallon (UK dry or liq.) according to the Imperial system of units divided by the SI unit
    minute

units.label: Gallon (UK) per Second
units.description:
unit gallon (UK dry or liq.) according to the Imperial system of units divided by the SI base unit
    second

units.label: Us Gallon
units.description: "US Gallon" is a unit for  'Liquid Volume' expressed as $galUS$.

units.label: Us Gallon per Day
units.description: "US Gallon per Day" is a unit for  'Volume Per Unit Time' expressed as $gal/d$.

units.label: Us Gallon per Hour
units.description: unit gallon (US, liq.) according to the Anglo-American system of units divided by the SI unit hour

units.label: Us Gallon per Minute
units.description: "US Gallon per Minute" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Volume Per Unit Time' expressed as $gal/min$.

units.description:
unit gallon (US, liq.) according to the Anglo-American system of units divided by the SI base unit
    second

units.label: Dry Gallon Us
units.description: "Dry Gallon US" is a unit for  'Dry Volume' expressed as $dry_gal$.

units.label: Gamma
units.description: "Gamma" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Magnetic Field'.

units.label: French Gauge
units.description:
unit for the diameter of thin tubes in the medical technology (e.g. catheter) and
    telecommunications engineering (e.g. fiberglasses).

units.label: Gauss
units.description: CGS unit of the magnetic flux density B

units.label: Charrière Gauge
units.description:
unit for the diameter of urological instruments and catheters for different purposes corresponding to: 1
    Ch = 0,333 333 333 10 ⁻ ³ m

units.label: Gilbert
units.description:
The fundamental unit of magnetomotive force ($mmf$) in electromagnetic units is called a Gilbert. It is
    the $mmf$ which will produce a magnetic field strength of one Gauss (Maxwell per Square Centimeter) in a path one centimeter
    long.

units.label: Gill (UK)
units.description: unit of the volume for fluids according to the Imperial system of units (1/32 Imperial Gallon)

units.label: Gill (UK) per Day
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (UK) for fluids according to the Imperial system of units divided by the
    unit for time day

units.label: Gill (UK) per Hour
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (UK) for fluids according to the Imperial system of units divided by the
    unit for time hour

units.label: Gill (UK) per Minute
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (UK) for fluids according to the Imperial system of units divided by the
    unit for time minute

units.label: Gill (UK) per Second
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (UK) for fluids according to the Imperial system of units divided by the SI
    base unit second

units.label: Gill (US)
units.description: unit of the volume according the Anglo-American system of units (1/32 US Gallon)

units.label: Gill (US) per Day
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (US) for fluids according to the Anglo-American system of units divided by
    the unit for time day

units.label: Gill (US) per Hour
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (US) for fluids according to the Anglo-American system of units divided by
    the unit for time hour

units.label: Gill (US) per Minute
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (US) for fluids according to the Anglo-American system of units divided by
    the unit for time minute

units.label: Gill (US) per Second
units.description:
unit of the volume gill (US) for fluids according to the Anglo-American system of units divided by
    the SI base unit second

units.label: Gram
units.description:
A unit of mass in the metric system. The name comes from the Greek gramma, a small weight identified in
    later Roman and Byzantine times with the Latin scripulum or scruple (the English scruple is equal to about 1.3 grams). The
    gram was originally defined to be the mass of one cubic centimeter of pure water, but to provide precise standards it was
    necessary to construct physical objects of specified mass. One gram is now defined to be 1/1000 of the mass of the standard
    kilogram, a platinum-iridium bar carefully guarded by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures in Paris for more than
    a century. (The kilogram, rather than the gram, is considered the base unit of mass in the SI.) The gram is a small mass,
    equal to about 15.432 grains or 0.035 273 966 ounce.

units.label: Gram Centimetre per Second
units.description:
product of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram and the 0.01-fold of the SI base unit metre
    divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Gram Hour per Litre Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and the 0.000001-fold of power of the
    SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per unit of time hour

units.label: Gram Hour per Litre Cubic Metre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and power of the SI base unit metre
    with the exponent 3 per unit of time hour

units.label: Gram Hour per Square Litre
units.description: quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and unit litre per unit of time hour

units.label: Gram Hour per Cubic Metre Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and the 0.000001-fold of power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per unit of time hour

units.label: Gram Hour per Cubic Metre Litre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and unit litre per unit of time hour

units.label: Gram Hour per Sextic Metre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per unit of time hour

units.label: Gram Minute per Litre Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and 0.000001-fold of power of the SI
    base unit metre with the exponent 3 per unit of time minute

units.label: Gram Minute per Litre Cubic Metre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and power of the SI base unit metre
    with the exponent 3 per unit of time minute

units.label: Gram Minute per Square Litre
units.description: quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and unit litre per unit of time minute

units.label: Gram Minute per Cubic Metre Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and 0.000001-fold of power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per unit of time minute

units.label: Gram Minute per Cubic Metre Litre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and unit litre per unit of time minute

units.label: Gram Minute per Sextic Metre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per unit of time minute

units.label: Gram Millimetre
units.description:
unit of the imbalance as product of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram and the 0.001-fold
    of the SI base unit metre

units.label: Gram per Bar
units.description: 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the unit bar

units.label: Gram per Centimetre Bar
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.000001-fold of the power of

units.label: Gram per Centimetre Second
units.description:
unit of the dynamic viscosity as a quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the

units.label: Gram per Square Centimetre

0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.0001-fold of the power of the SI base unit
    metre and exponent 2

units.label: Gram per Square Centimetre Year
units.description:
A rate of change of 0.001 of the SI unit of mass over 0.00001 of the SI unit of area in a period of an
    average calendar year (365.25 days)

units.label: Gram per Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.000001-fold of the power of the SI base
    unit metre with the exponent 3

units.label: Gram per Cubic Centimetre Bar
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.000001-fold of the power of
    the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 and the unit bar

units.label: Gram per Cubic Centimetre Kelvin
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.000001-fold of the power of
    the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 and the SI base unit kelvin

units.label: Gram per Day
units.description: 0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the unit day

units.label: Gram per Day Bar

units.label: Gram per Day Kelvin
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the unit day and the SI base unit

units.label: Gram per Degree Celsius
units.description:
$\textit{Gram Degree Celsius}$ is a C.G.S System unit for 'Mass Temperature' expressed as $g \cdot
    degC$.

units.label: Gram per Decilitre
units.description: A derived unit for amount-of-substance concentration measured in g/dL.

units.label: Gram per Cubic Decimetre

0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.001-fold of the power of the SI base unit

units.label: Gram per Cubic Decimetre Bar

0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.001-fold of the power of the

units.label: Gram per Gram
units.description:
mass ratio consisting of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.001-fold of the SI
    base unit kilogram.

units.label: Gram per Hectare
units.description:
Gram Per Hectare is a unit of mass per area. Gram Per Hectare (mg/ha) has a dimension of ML-3 where M is
    mass, and L is length. It can be converted to the corresponding standard SI unit kg/m2 by multiplying its value by a factor of
    0.0000001.

units.label: Gram per Hour
units.description: 0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the unit hour

units.label: Gram per Hour Bar
units.description: 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the unit hour and the unit bar

units.label: Gram per Hour Kelvin
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the unit hour and the SI base unit
    kelvin

units.label: Gram per Hertz
units.description: 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the SI derived unit hertz

units.label: Gram per Hectogram
units.description: 0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by 0.1-fold of the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Gram per Kelvin
units.description: 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the SI base unit kelvin

units.label: Gram per Kilogram
units.description: 0,001 fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Gram per Kilometre

units.label: Gram per Litre

units.label: Gram per Litre Bar

units.label: Gram per Litre Centipoise

[CGS] quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and and the 0.01-fold of the CGS
    unit of the dynamic viscosity poise

units.label: Gram per Litre Kelvin

0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the unit litre and the SI base unit
    kelvin

units.label: Gram per Litre Millipascal Second

quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and the product of the 0.001-fold of

units.label: Gram per Square Metre Day
units.description:
A metric unit of volume over time indicating the amount generated across one square meter over a
    day.

units.label: Gram per Square Metre Hour
units.description:
0.0001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the SI base unit meter with the exponent 2 over
    a period of 1 hour

units.label: Gram per Square Metre Year
units.description:
A metric unit of volume over time indicating the amount generated across one square meter over a
    year.

units.label: Gram per Cubic Metre

0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the

units.label: Gram per Cubic Metre Bar
