0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the power of the SI base unit metre
    with the exponent 3 and the SI base unit kelvin

units.label: Gram per Cubic Metre Millipascal Second
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and the product of the 0.001-fold of the SI derived unit pascal and the SI base unit second

units.label: Gram per Cubic Metre Pascal Second
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and the product of the SI derived unit pascal and the SI base unit second

units.label: Gram per Cubic Metre Poise
units.description:
[CGS] quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with
    the exponent 3 and the CGS unit of the dynamic viscosity poise

units.label: Gram per Minute
units.description: 0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the unit minute

units.label: Gram per Minute Bar
units.description: 0.001-fold the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the unit minute and the unit bar

units.label: Gram per Minute Kelvin
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the unit minute and the SI base
    unit kelvin

units.label: Gram per Mole
units.description: 0.01-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the SI base unit mol

units.label: Gram per Millilitre
units.description: 0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.001-fold of the unit litre

units.label: Gram per Millilitre Bar
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.001-fold of the unit litre
    and the unit bar

units.label: Gram per Millilitre Kelvin
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.001-fold of the unit litre
    and the SI base unit kelvin

units.label: Gram per Millimetre
units.description: 0,001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.001-fold the SI base unit meter

units.label: Gram per Millimetre Bar
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.001-fold of the unit meter
    and the unit bar

units.label: Gram per Square Millimetre
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.000001-fold of the power of the SI base unit
    meter by exponent 2

units.label: Gram per Second
units.description: 0,001fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Gram per Second Bar
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the SI base unit second and the
    unit bar

units.label: Gram per Second Kelvin
units.description:
0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the SI base unit second and the SI
    base unit kelvin

units.label: Gram Second per Litre Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and the 0.000001-fold of power of the
    SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per SI base unit second

units.label: Gram Second per Litre Cubic Metre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and power of the SI base unit metre
    with the exponent 3 per SI base unit second

units.label: Gram Second per Square Litre
units.description: quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per litre and unit litre per SI base unit second

units.label: Gram Second per Cubic Metre Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and the 0.000001-fold of power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per SI base unit second

units.label: Gram Second per Cubic Metre Litre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and unit litre per SI base unit second

units.label: Gram Second per Sextic Metre
units.description:
quotient of the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram per power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 and power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3 per SI base unit second

units.label: Gram of Carbon per Square Metre Day
units.description:
A metric unit of volume over time indicating the amount generated across one square meter over a
    day. Used to express productivity of an ecosystem.

units.label: Gram Force
units.description: "Gram Force" is a unit for  'Force' expressed as $gf$.

units.label: Gram Force per Square Centimetre
units.description: A non-SI-conforming unit of pressure

units.label: Gram of Nitrogen per Square Metre Day
units.description:
A metric unit of volume over time indicating the amount of Nitrogen generated across one square
    meter over a day. Used to express productivity of an ecosystem.

units.label: Gon
units.description: "Gon" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Plane Angle' expressed as $gon$.

units.label: Grade
units.description: the tangent of an angle of inclination multiplied by 100

units.label: Grad
units.description: "Grad" is a unit for  'Plane Angle' expressed as $grad$.

units.label: Grain
units.description:
A grain is a unit of measurement of mass that is nominally based upon the mass of a single seed of a
    cereal.  The grain is the only unit of mass measure common to the three traditional English mass and weight systems; the
    obsolete Tower grain was, by definition, exactly  /64 of a troy grain. Since 1958, the grain or troy grain measure has been
    defined in terms of units of mass in the International System of Units as precisely 64.79891 milligrams. Thus, $1 gram
    \approx 15.4323584 grains$.  There are precisely 7,000 grains per avoirdupois pound in the imperial and U.S. customary units,
    and 5,760 grains in the Troy pound.

units.label: Grain per Imperial Gallon
units.description: "Grain per Imperial Gallon" is an Imperial unit for  'Density' expressed as $gr/gal$.

units.label: Grain per Us Gallon
units.description: unit of the density according to the Anglo-American system of units

units.label: Grain per Pound Mass
units.description:
Grains per pound-mass, a dimensionless mass-ratio unit. One grain is 1/7000 of an avoirdupois pound, so 1
    gr/lb = 1/7000 kg/kg.

units.label: Grain per Cubic Metre
units.description: Grains per cubic metre of volume

units.label: Gray
units.description:
The SI unit of radiation dose. Radiation carries energy, and when it is absorbed by matter the matter
    receives this energy. The dose is the amount of energy deposited per unit of mass. One gray is defined to be the dose of one
    joule of energy absorbed per kilogram of matter, or 100 rad. The unit is named for the British physician L. Harold Gray
    (1905-1965), an authority on the use of radiation in the treatment of cancer.

units.label: Gray per Hour
units.description: SI derived unit gray divided by the unit hour

units.label: Gray per Minute
units.description: SI derived unit gray divided by the unit minute

units.label: Gray per Second
units.description: "Gray per Second" is a unit for  'Absorbed Dose Rate' expressed as $Gy/s$.

units.label: Gross Tonnage
units.description:
Gross tonnage (GT, G.T. or gt) is a nonlinear measure of a ship's overall internal volume. Gross
    tonnage is different from gross register tonnage. Gross tonnage is used to determine things such as a ship's manning
    regulations, safety rules, registration fees, and port dues, whereas the older gross register tonnage is a measure of the
    volume of only certain enclosed spaces.

units.label: Gamma
units.description: "Gamma" is a C.G.S System unit for  'Magnetic Field'.

units.label: Gibibit
units.description: 1,073,741,824-fold of the unit bit

units.label: Gibibit per Metre
units.description: 1,073,741,824-fold of the unit bit divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Gibibit per Square Metre
units.description: 1,073,741,824-fold of the unit bit divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 2

units.label: Gibibit per Cubic Metre
units.description: 1,073,741,824-fold of the unit bit divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3

units.label: Gibibyte
units.description: The gibibyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information storage. The prefix gibi means 1024^3

units.label: Gigaampere
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the unit ampere

units.label: Gigabit
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the unit bit

units.label: Gigabit per Metre
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the unit bit divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Gigabit per Second
units.description:
A gigabit per second (Gbit/s or Gb/s) is a unit of data transfer rate equal to 1,000,000,000 bits per
    second.

units.label: Gigabecquerel
units.description: 1 000 000 000-fold of the derived SI unit becquerel

units.label: Gigabyte
units.description:
The gigabyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information storage. The prefix giga means $10^9$
    in the International System of Units (SI), therefore 1 gigabyte is $1,000,000,000 \; bytes$. The unit symbol for the gigabyte
    is $GB$ or $Gbyte$, but not $Gb$ (lower case b) which is typically used for the gigabit. Historically, the term has also been
    used in some fields of computer science and information technology to denote the $gibibyte$, or $1073741824 \; bytes$.

units.label: Gigabyte per Second
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the unit byte divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Giga Base Pair
units.description:
A gigabase (abbreviated Gb, or Gbp for gigabase pairs.) is a unit of measurement used to help
    designate the length of DNA. One gigabase is equal to 1 billion bases.

units.label: Gigacoulomb per Cubic Metre
units.description:
1 000 000 000-fold of the SI derived unit coulomb divided by the power of the SI base unit metre
    with the exponent 3

units.label: Giga Electron Volt
units.description: "Giga Electron Volt" is a unit for  'Energy And Work' expressed as $GeV$.

units.label: Giga Floating Point Operations per Second
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the unit floating point operations divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Gigahertz
units.description:
The hertz (symbol Hz) is the SI unit of frequency defined as the number of cycles per second of a
    periodic phenomenon. A GigaHertz is $10^{9} hz$.

units.label: Gigahertz Metre
units.description: product of the 1 000 000 000-fold of the SI derived unit hertz and the SI base unit metre

units.label: Gigajoule
units.description: 1 000 000 000-fold of the SI derived unit joule

units.label: Gigajoule per Hour
units.description: SI derived unit gigajoule divided by the 3600 times the SI base unit second

units.label: Gigajoule per Square Metre
units.description:
Gigajoule Per Square Meter ($J/m^2$) is a unit in the category of Energy density. It is also known as
    Gigajoules per square meter, Gigajoule per square metre, Gigajoule/square meter, Gigajoule/square metre.

units.label: Gigajoule per Second
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the SI derived unit joule divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Giganewton Metre per Square Metre
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the SI derived unit newton divided by the SI base unit metre to the power two

units.label: Gigaohm
units.description: 1 000 000 000-fold of the SI derived unit ohm

units.label: Gigaohm Metre
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the product out of the SI derived unit ohm and the SI unit metre

units.label: Gigaohm per Metre
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the SI derived unit ohm divided by the SI unit metre

units.label: Gigapascal
units.description: 1 000 000 000-fold of the SI derived unit pascal

units.label: Gigavolt
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the SI derived unit volt

units.label: Gigavolt Ampere
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the product of the SI base unit volt with the SI base unit ampere

units.label: GigaVolt Ampere Reactive
units.description: 0.000000001 of the unit volt ampere reactive

units.label: Giga Volt Ampere
units.description: 1,000,000,000-fold of the product of the SI base unit volt with the SI base unit ampere

units.label: Giga Volt Ampere Reactive
units.description: 0.000000001 of the unit volt ampere reactive

units.label: Gigawatt
units.description: 1 000 000 000-fold of the SI derived unit watt

units.label: Gigawatt Hour
units.description: 1 000 000 000-fold of the product of the SI derived unit watt and the unit hour

units.label: Gigawatt Hour per Square Foot
units.description:
A unit of energy per unit area, equivalent to approximately 38,750,077,500,155 joules per square
    metre.

units.label: Gigawatt Hour per Square Metre
units.description: A unit of energy per unit area, equivalent to 3,600,000,000,000 joules per square metre.

units.label: Gs
units.description:
The $gauss$, abbreviated as $G$, is the cgs unit of measurement of a magnetic field $B$,
  which is also known as the "magnetic flux density" or the "magnetic induction".
  One gauss is defined as one maxwell per square centimeter; it equals $10^{-4} tesla$ (or $100 micro T$).
  The Gauss is identical to maxwells per square centimetre; technically defined in a three-dimensional system,
  it corresponds in the SI, with its extra base unit the ampere.
  The gauss is quite small by earthly standards, 1 Gs being only about four times Earth's flux density,
  but it is subdivided, with $1 gauss = 105 gamma$.
  This unit of magnetic induction is also known as the $\textit{abtesla}$.

units.label: Henry
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Henry}$ is the SI unit of electric inductance. A changing magnetic field induces an
    electric current in a loop of wire (or in a coil of many loops) located in the field. Although the induced voltage depends
    only on the rate at which the magnetic flux changes, measured in webers per second, the amount of the current depends also on
    the physical properties of the coil. A coil with an inductance of one henry requires a flux of one weber for each ampere of
    induced current. If, on the other hand, it is the current which changes, then the induced field will generate a potential
    difference within the coil: if the inductance is one henry a current change of one ampere per second generates a potential
    difference of one volt. The henry is a large unit; inductances in practical circuits are measured in millihenrys (mH) or
    microhenrys (u03bc H). The unit is named for the American physicist Joseph Henry (1797-1878), one of several scientists who
    discovered independently how magnetic fields can be used to generate alternating currents.  A $\textit{Henry}$ is defined as:
    $$\text{H} \; \equiv \; \text{henry}\; \equiv\; \frac{\text{Wb}}{\text{A}}\; \equiv\;
    \frac{\text{weber}}{\text{amp}}\; \equiv\ \frac{\text{V}\cdot\text{s}}{\text{A}}\; \equiv\; \frac{\text{volt}
    \cdot \text{second}}{\text{amp}}\; \equiv\ \Omega\cdot\text{s}\; \equiv\; \text{ohm.second}$$

units.label: Henry per Kiloohm
units.description: SI derived unit henry divided by the 1 000-fold of the SI derived unit ohm

units.label: Henry per Metre
units.description:
The henry per meter (symbolized $H/m$) is the unit of magnetic permeability in the International System
    of Units ( SI ). Reduced to base units in SI, $1\,H/m$ is the equivalent of one kilogram meter per square second per square
    ampere.

units.label: Henry per Ohm
units.description: SI derived unit henry divided by the SI derived unit ohm

units.label: Hectare
units.description:
The customary metric unit of land area, equal to 100 ares. One hectare is a square hectometer, that is,
    the area of a square 100 meters on each side: exactly 10 000 square meters or approximately 107 639.1 square feet, 11 959.9
    square yards, or 2.471 054 acres.

units.label: Hartley
units.description: The "Hartley" is a unit of information.

units.label: Hartley per Second
units.description: The "Hartley per Second" is a unit of information rate.

units.label: Hefner-kerze
units.description: obsolete, non-legal unit of the power in Germany relating to DIN 1301-3:1979

units.label: Horsepower
units.description: 550 foot-pound force per second

units.label: Boiler Horsepower
units.description: "Boiler Horsepower" is a unit for  'Power' expressed as $hp_boiler$.

units.label: Horsepower (brake)
units.description: unit of the power according to the Imperial system of units

units.label: Horsepower (electric)
units.description: unit of the power according to the Anglo-American system of units

units.label: Horsepower (water)
units.description: unit of the power according to the Anglo-American system of units

units.label: Horsepower (metric)
units.description: unit of the mechanical power according to the Anglo-American system of units

units.label: Hour
units.description:
The hour (common symbol: h or h) is a unit of measurement of time. In modern usage, an hour comprises 60
    minutes, or 3,600 seconds. It is approximately 1/24 of a mean solar day. An hour in the Universal Coordinated Time (UTC) time
    standard can include a negative or positive leap second, and may therefore have a duration of 3,599 or 3,601 seconds for
    adjustment purposes. Although it is not a standard defined by the International System of Units, the hour is a unit accepted
    for use with SI, represented by the symbol h.

units.label: Hour Square Foot
units.description: "Hour Square Foot" is an Imperial unit for  'Area Time' expressed as $hr-ft^{2}$.

units.label: Hour per Square Foot
units.description:
quotient of the unit of the mass avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per power
    of the unit foot according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the exponent 3 and unit of the mass
    avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois system of units per product of foot according to the Anglo-American and the
    Imperial system of units and unit of time hour

units.label: Hour per Year
units.description: hours (of activity) per year

units.label: Sidereal Hour
units.description:
Sidereal time is a time-keeping system astronomers use to keep track of the direction to point their
    telescopes to view a given star in the night sky. A mean sidereal day is about 23 h 56 m 4.1 s in length. However, due to
    variations in the rotation rate of the Earth, the rate of an ideal sidereal clock deviates from any simple multiple of a civil
    clock. In practice, the difference is kept track of by the difference UTC-UT1, which is measured by radio telescopes and kept
    on file and available to the public at the IERS and at the United States Naval Observatory. A Sidereal Hour is $1/24^{th}$ of
    a Sidereal Day. A mean sidereal day is 23 hours, 56 minutes, 4.0916 seconds (23.9344699 hours or 0.99726958 mean solar days),
    the time it takes Earth to make one rotation relative to the vernal equinox. (Due to nutation, an actual sidereal day is not
    quite so constant.) The vernal equinox itself precesses slowly westward relative to the fixed stars, completing one revolution
    in about 26,000 years, so the misnamed sidereal day ("sidereal" is derived from the Latin sidus meaning "star") is 0.0084
    seconds shorter than Earth's period of rotation relative to the fixed stars.

units.label: Hundred
units.description: Counting unit for a count of one hundred

units.label: Hertz
units.description:
$\textit{Hertz}$ (symbol $Hz$) is the SI unit of frequency defined as the number of cycles per second of
    a periodic phenomenon. One of its most common uses is the description of the sine wave, particularly those used in radio and
    audio applications, such as the frequency of musical tones. The word $\bf{hertz}$ is named for Heinrich Rudolf Hertz, who was
    the first to conclusively prove the existence of electromagnetic waves.

units.label: Hertz Metre
units.description: product of the SI derived unit hertz and the SI base unit metre

units.label: Hertz per Kelvin
units.description: $\textit{Hertz per Kelvin}$ is a unit for 'Inverse Time Temperature' expressed as $Hz K^{-1}$.

units.label: Hertz per Second
units.description: $\textit{Hertz per Second}$ is a unit for 'Rate of Change of Frequency' expressed as $Hz s^{-1}$.

units.label: Hertz per Tesla
units.description: "Hertz per Tesla" is a unit for  'Electric Charge Per Mass' expressed as $Hz T^{-1}$.

units.label: Hertz per Volt
units.description:
In the Hertz per Volt standard the frequency of the note is directly related to the voltage. A pitch of a
    note goes up one octave when its frequency doubles, meaning that the voltage will have to double for every octave rise.
    Depending on the footage (octave) selected, nominally one volt gives 1000Hz, two volts 2000Hz and so on. In terms of notes,
    bottom C would be 0.25 volts, the next C up would be 0.5 volts, then 1V, 2V, 4V, 8V for the following octaves. This system was
    used mainly by Yamaha and Korg.

units.label: Abhenry
units.description:
Abhenry is the centimeter-gram-second electromagnetic unit of inductance, equal to one billionth of a
    henry.

units.label: Stathenry
units.description:
The $\text{Stathenry (statH)}$ is a unit in the category of Electric inductance.
  It is also known as $tathenries$.
  This unit is commonly used in the cgs unit system.
  $Stathenry$ has a dimension of $ML^2T^{-2}I^{-2}$ where $M$ is mass, $L$ is length, $T$ is time, and $I$ is electric current.
  It can be converted to the corresponding standard SI unit H by multiplying its value by a factor of $8.987552 \times 10^{11}$.

units.label: Stathenry per Centimetre
units.description: The Stathenry per Centimeter is a unit of measure for the absolute permeability of free space.

units.label: Heart Beat
units.description:
A heart beat is a single contraction of the heart muscle,
  which pumps blood through the circulatory system. The heart rate is the number of heart beats
  per unit of time, typically measured in beats per minute (bpm). A normal resting
  heart rate for adults ranges from 60 to 100 beats per minute.

units.label: Hectobar
units.description: 100-fold of the unit bar

units.label: Hectocoulomb
units.description: "HectoCoulomb" is a unit for  'Electric Charge' expressed as $hC$.

units.label: Hectogram
units.description: 0.1-fold of the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Hectohertz
units.description: 100-fold of the SI derived unit hertz

units.label: Hectolitre
units.description: 100-fold of the unit litre

units.label: Hectometre
units.description: 100-fold of the SI base unit metre

units.label: Hectopascal
units.description:
Hectopascal is a unit of pressure. 1 Pa is approximately the pressure exerted by a 10-g mass resting on a
    1-cm2 area. 1013 hPa = 1 atm. There are 100 pascals in 1 hectopascal.

units.label: Hectopascal Litre per Second
units.description:
product out of the 100-fold of the SI derived unit pascal and the unit litre divided by the SI base
    unit second

units.label: Hectopascal Cubic Metre per Second
units.description:
product out of the 100-fold of the SI unit pascal and the power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3 divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Hectopascal per Bar
units.description: 100-fold of the SI derived unit pascal divided by the unit bar

units.label: Hectopascal per Hour
units.description:
A change in pressure of one hundred Newtons per square metre (100 Pascals) per hour. Equivalent to a
    change of one millibar per hour.

units.label: Hectopascal per Kelvin
units.description: 100-fold of the SI derived unit pascal divided by the SI base unit kelvin

units.label: Hectopascal per Metre
units.description: 100-fold of the SI derived unit pascal divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Hundredweight (UK)
units.description: out of use unit of the mass according to the Imperial system of units

units.label: Hundredweight (US)
units.description: out of use unit of the mass according to the Imperial system of units

units.label: Inch
units.description:
An inch is the name of a unit of length in a number of different systems, including Imperial units, and
    United States customary units. There are 36 inches in a yard and 12 inches in a foot. Corresponding units of area and volume
    are the square inch and the cubic inch.

units.label: Inch Poundal
units.description:
Unit of work (force multiplied by path) according to the Imperial system of units as a product unit inch
    multiplied by poundal. Product of the non SI-conform unit of the force poundal and the unit inch according to the
    Anglo-American and Imperial system of units.

units.label: Inch per 2pirad
units.description:
unit of the translation factor for implementation from rotation to linear move according to the
    Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units

units.label: Inch per Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units divided by the unit for
    temperature degree Fahrenheit

units.label: Inch per Minute
units.description:
The inch per minute is a unit of speed or velocity. It expresses the distance in inches (in) traveled or
    displaced, divided by time in minutes (min). The equivalent SI unit is the metre per second.

units.label: Inch per Psi
units.description:
unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units divided by the composed unit
    for pressure (pound-force per square inch)

units.label: Inch per Revolution
units.description:
unit of the translation factor for implementation from rotation to linear move according to the
    Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units

units.label: Inch per Second
units.description:
The inch per second is a unit of speed or velocity. It expresses the distance in inches (in) traveled or
    displaced, divided by time in seconds (s, or sec). The equivalent SI unit is the metre per second. Abbreviations include in/s,
    in/sec, ips, and less frequently in s.

units.label: Inch per Second Degree Fahrenheit
units.description:
unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units divided by the product of the
    SI base unit second and the traditional unit degree Fahrenheit

units.label: Inch per Second Psi
units.description:
quotient of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units and the SI
    base unit second divided by the composed unit for pressure (pound-force per square inch)

units.label: Inch per Square Second
units.description:
$\textit{Inch per Square second}$ is an Imperial unit for $\textit{Linear Acceleration}$ expressed as
    $in/s^2$.

units.label: Inch per Year
units.description:
unit of the length according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system of units divided by the unit
    common year with 365 days

units.label: Square Inch
units.description:
A square inch is a unit of area, equal to the area of a square with sides of one inch. The following
    symbols are used to denote square inches: square in, sq inches, sq inch, sq in inches/-2, inch/-2, in/-2, inches^2, $inch^2$,
    $in^2$, $inches^2$, $inch^2$, $in^2$ or in some cases $"^2$. The square inch is a common unit of measurement in the United
    States and the United Kingdom.

units.label: Square Inch per Second
units.description:
power of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the
    exponent 2 divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Cubic Inch
units.description:
The cubic inch is a unit of measurement for volume in the Imperial units and United States customary
    units systems. It is the volume of a cube with each of its three sides being one inch long. The cubic inch and the cubic foot
    are still used as units of volume in the United States, although the common SI units of volume, the liter, milliliter, and
    cubic meter, are continually replacing them, especially in manufacturing and high technology. One cubic foot is equal to
    exactly 1728 cubic inches.

units.label: Cubic Inch per Hour
units.description:
power of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the
    exponent 3 divided by the unit hour

units.label: Cubic Inch per Pound Mass
units.description:
power of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system of units by exponent 3 divided
    by the avoirdupois pound according to the avoirdupois unit system

units.label: Cubic Inch per Minute
units.description: "Cubic Inch per Minute" is an Imperial unit for  'Volume Per Unit Time' expressed as $in^{3}/min$.

units.label: Cubic Inch per Second
units.description:
power of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the
    exponent 3 divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Quartic Inch
units.description:
power of the unit inch according to the Anglo-American and the Imperial system of units with the
    exponent 4

units.label: Inch of Water
units.description:
Inches of water, wc, inch water column (inch WC), inAq, Aq, or inH2O is a non-SI unit for pressure. The
    units are by convention and due to the historical measurement of certain pressure differentials. It is used for measuring
    small pressure differences across an orifice, or in a pipeline or shaft. Inches of water can be converted to a pressure unit
    using the formula for pressure head. It is defined as the pressure exerted by a column of water of 1 inch in height at defined
    conditions for example $39 ^\circ F$ at the standard acceleration of gravity; 1 inAq is approximately equal to 249 pascals at
    $0 ^\circ C$.

units.label: Inch of Water (39.2 °F)
units.description:
non SI-conform unit of pressure according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system for units, whereas
    the value of 1 inH₂O meets the static pressure, which is generated by a head of water at a temperature of 39.2°F with a height
    of 1 inch

units.label: Inch of Water (60 °F)
units.description:
non SI-conform unit of pressure according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system for units, whereas
    the value of 1 inH₂O meets the static pressure, which is generated by a head of water at a temperature of 60°F with a height
    of 1 inch

units.label: Inch of Mercury
units.description:
Inches of mercury, (inHg) is a unit of measurement for pressure. It is still widely used for barometric
    pressure in weather reports, refrigeration and aviation in the United States, but is seldom used elsewhere. It is defined as
    the pressure exerted by a column of mercury of 1 inch in height at $32 ^\circ F$ at the standard acceleration of gravity. 1
    inHg = 3,386.389 pascals at $0 ^\circ C$.

units.label: Inch of Mercury (32 °F)
units.description:
non SI-conform unit of pressure according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system for units, whereas
    the value of 1 inHg meets the static pressure, which is generated by a mercury at a temperature of 32°F with a height of 1
    inch

units.label: Inch of Mercury (60 °F)
units.description:
non SI-conform unit of pressure according to the Anglo-American and Imperial system for units, whereas
    the value of 1 inHg meets the static pressure, which is generated by a mercury at a temperature of 60°F with a height of 1
    inch

units.label: International Unit
units.description:
The $\textit{International Unit}$ ($IU$) is a substance-dependent reference unit of biological activity used in
   pharmacology. For any given substance, one $IU$ is defined as the activity of a fixed mass of an international
   reference preparation (e.g. a WHO International Standard), so a conversion to mass exists but differs from one
   substance to another; it is therefore resolved at the level of a concrete quantity rather than stated here
   (hence $conversionMultiplier = 0.0$). For this reason the unit is dimensioned as mass ($M$) and modelled as a
   mass-equivalent, not as amount of substance ($N$): one $IU$ is not a fixed number of moles. This follows the same
   pattern QUDT uses for other substance-dependent equivalents (e.g. mass equivalent, CO2 equivalent), where the
   base dimension is retained and the per-substance factor is pinned at the quantity level.

units.label: International Unit per Litre
units.description:
The $\textit{International Unit per Liter}$ is a unit for 'Serum Or Plasma Level' expressed as $IU/L$.
The magnitude of one $IU/L$ depends on the material, so there is no single conversion multiplier.
Following the mass-equivalent treatment of $IU$ (see unit:IU), this is dimensioned as a mass concentration.

units.label: International Unit per Milligram
units.description: International Units per milligramme.

units.label: International Unit per Millilitre
units.description:
The $\textit{International Unit per Milliliter}$ is a unit for  'Serum Or Plasma Level' expressed as $IU/mL$.
The magnitude of one $IU/L$ depends on the material, so there is no single conversion multiplier.
Following the mass-equivalent treatment of $IU$ (see unit:IU), this is dimensioned as a mass concentration.

units.label: Joule
units.description:
The SI unit of work or energy, defined to be the work done by a force of one newton acting to move
    an object through a distance of one meter in the direction in which the force is applied. Equivalently, since kinetic energy
    is one half the mass times the square of the velocity, one joule is the kinetic energy of a mass of two kilograms moving at a
    velocity of 1 m/s. This is the same as 107 ergs in the CGS system, or approximately 0.737 562 foot-pound in the traditional
    English system. In other energy units, one joule equals about 9.478 170 x 10-4 Btu, 0.238 846 (small) calories, or 2.777 778 x
    10-4 watt hour. The joule is named for the British physicist James Prescott Joule (1818-1889), who demonstrated the
    equivalence of mechanical and thermal energy in a famous experiment in 1843.

units.label: Joule Metre per Mole
units.description:
$\textit{Joule Meter per Mole}$ is a unit for 'Length Molar Energy' expressed as:
  $$J \cdot m \cdot mol^{-1}$$.

units.label: Joule per Square Centimetre
units.description:
derived SI unit joule divided by the 0.0001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre by exponent
    2

units.label: Joule per Square Centimetre Day
units.description: Radiant energy per 10^-4 SI unit area over a period of one day.

units.label: Joule per Cubic Centimetre Kelvin
units.description: Joule per Cubic Centimeter Kelvin is a unit for Volumetric Heat Capacity expressed as J/(cm³·K)

units.label: Joule per Day
units.description: quotient from the SI derived unit joule divided by the unit day

units.label: Joule per Gram
units.description: SI derived unit joule divided by the 0.001-fold of the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Joule per Gram Degree Celsius
units.description: Unit for expressing the specific heat capacity.

units.label: Joule per Gram Kelvin
units.description: Unit for expressing the specific heat capacity.

units.label: Joule per Hour
units.description: SI derived unit joule divided by the 3600 times the SI base unit second

units.label: Joule per Kelvin
units.description:
Joule Per Kelvin (J/K) is a unit in the category of Entropy. It is also known as joules per kelvin,
    joule/kelvin. This unit is commonly used in the SI unit system. Joule Per Kelvin (J/K) has a dimension of $ML^{2}T^{-2}Q^{-1}$
    where $M$ is mass, $L$ is length, $T$ is time, and Q is temperature. This unit is the standard SI unit in this category.

units.label: Joule per Kilogram
units.description:
A $\textit{Joule Per Kilogram}$, ($J/kg$), is a unit in the category of total energy per unit mass,
    commonly known as specific enthalpy. It is also known as $\textit{joules per kilogram}$. The unit has a dimension of
    $L2T^{-2}$ where $L$ is length, and $T$ is time. This unit is the standard SI unit in this category.

units.label: Joule per Kilogram Degree Celsius
units.description: Unit for expressing the specific heat capacity.

units.label: Joule per Kilogram Kelvin
units.description:
Specific heat capacity - The heat required to raise unit mass of a substance by unit temperature interval
    under specified conditions, such as constant pressure: usually measured in joules per kelvin per kilogram. Symbol $c_p$ (for
    constant pressure). Also called specific heat.

units.label: Joule per Kilogram Kelvin Cubic Metre
Joule per Square Metre
units.description:
Joule Per Square Meter ($J/m^2$) is a unit in the category of Energy density. It is also known as joules
    per square meter, joule per square metre, joule/square meter, joule/square metre. This unit is commonly used in the SI unit
    system.

units.label: Joules per Meter Squared Sqrt(second) Degree Kelvin
units.description:
A unit of thermal inertia measured as Joules per meter squared per square root Seconds per degree
    Kelvin

units.label: Joules per Meter Squared Sqrt(second) Degree Kelvin
units.description:
A unit of thermal inertia measured as Joules per meter squared per square root Seconds per degree
    Kelvin

units.label: Joule per Cubic Metre
units.description:
$\textit{Joule Per Cubic Meter}$ ($J/m^{3}$) is a unit in the category of Energy density. It is also
    known as joules per cubic meter, joule per cubic metre, joules per cubic metre, joule/cubic meter, joule/cubic metre. This
    unit is commonly used in the SI unit system.  It has a dimension of $ML^{-1}T^{-2}$ where $M$ is mass, $L$ is length, and $T$
    is time. This unit is the standard SI unit in this category.

units.label: Joule per Cubic Metre Kelvin
units.description:
$\textit{Joule per Cubic Meter Kelvin}$ is a unit for 'Volumetric Heat Capacity' expressed as $J/(m^{3}
    K)$.

units.label: Joule per Quartic Metre
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Joule Per Quartic Meter}$ ($J/m^4$) is a unit for the spectral concentration of
    radiant energy density (in terms of wavelength), or the spectral radiant energy density (in terms of wave length). This unit
    is commonly used in the SI unit system.

units.label: Joule per Minute
units.description: quotient from the SI derived unit joule divided by the unit minute

units.label: Joule per Mole
units.description:
The joule per mole (symbol: $J\cdot mol^{-1}$) is an SI derived unit of energy per amount of material.
    Energy is measured in joules, and the amount of material is measured in moles. Physical quantities measured in $J\cdot
    mol^{-1}$) usually describe quantities of energy transferred during phase transformations or chemical reactions. Division by
    the number of moles facilitates comparison between processes involving different quantities of material and between similar
    processes involving different types of materials. The meaning of such a quantity is always context-dependent and, particularly
    for chemical reactions, is dependent on the (possibly arbitrary) definition of a 'mole' for a particular process.

units.label: Joule per Mole Kelvin
units.description:
Energy needed to heat one mole of substance by 1 Kelvin, under standard conditions (not standard
    temperature and pressure STP). The standard molar entropy is usually given the symbol S, and has units of joules per mole
    kelvin ( $ J\cdot mol^{-1} K^{-1}$). Unlike standard enthalpies of formation, the value of S is an absolute. That is, an
    element in its standard state has a nonzero value of S at room temperature.

units.label: Joule per Second
units.description: SI derived unit joule divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Joule per Tesla
units.description:
The magnetic moment of a magnet is a quantity that determines the force that the magnet can exert on
    electric currents and the torque that a magnetic field will exert on it. A loop of electric current, a bar magnet, an
    electron, a molecule, and a planet all have magnetic moments. The unit for magnetic moment is not a base unit in the
    International System of Units (SI) and it can be represented in more than one way. For example, in the current loop
    definition, the area is measured in square meters and I is measured in amperes, so the magnetic moment is measured in
    ampere-square meters (A m2). In the equation for torque on a moment, the torque is measured in joules and the magnetic field
    in tesla, so the moment is measured in Joules per Tesla (J u00b7T-1). These two representations are equivalent: 1 A u00b7m2 =
    1 J u00b7T-1.

units.label: Joule per Square Tesla
units.description: A measure of the diamagnetic energy, for a Bohr-radius spread around a magnetic axis, per square Tesla.

units.label: Joule Second
units.description:
The $\textit{joule-second}$ is a unit equal to a $joule$ multiplied by a second, used to measure action.
  The joule-second is the unit used for Planck's constant.

units.label: Joule Second per Mole
units.description: $\textit{Joule Second per Mole}$ is a unit for 'Molar Angular Momentum' expressed as $J s mol^{-1}$.

units.label: Kelvin
units.description:
The unit $\textit{Kelvin}$ is the SI base unit of temperature, previously called the degree Kelvin. One
    kelvin represents the same temperature difference as one degree Celsius. In 1967 the General Conference on Weights and
    Measures defined the temperature of the triple point of water (the temperature at which water exists simultaneously in the
    gaseous, liquid, and solid states) to be exactly 273.16 kelvins. Since this temperature is also equal to 0.01 u00b0C, the
    temperature in kelvins is always equal to 273.15 plus the temperature in degrees Celsius. The kelvin equals exactly 1.8
    degrees Fahrenheit. The unit is named for the British mathematician and physicist William Thomson (1824-1907), later known as
    Lord Kelvin after he was named Baron Kelvin of Largs.

units.label: Kelvin Metre per Watt
units.description: product of the SI base unit kelvin and the SI base unit metre divided by the derived SI unit watt

units.label: Kelvin Square Metre per Kilogram Second
Kelvin per Bar
units.description: SI base unit kelvin divided by the unit bar

units.label: Kelvin per Hour
units.description: $\textit{Kelvin per Hour}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Time' expressed as $K / h$.

units.label: Kelvin per Kelvin
units.description: SI base unit kelvin divided by the SI base unit kelvin

units.label: Kelvin per Metre
units.description: A change of temperature on the Kelvin temperature scale in one SI unit of length.

units.label: Kelvin per Minute
units.description: $\textit{Kelvin per Minute}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Time' expressed as $K / m$.

units.label: Kelvin per Pascal
units.description: SI base unit kelvin divided by the SI derived unit pascal

units.label: Kelvin per Second
units.description: $\textit{Kelvin per Second}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Time' expressed as $K / s$.

units.label: Kelvin per Square Second
units.description: $\textit{Kelvin per Square Second}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Time Squared' expressed as $K / s^2$.

units.label: Kelvin per Tesla
units.description:
$\textit{Kelvin per Tesla}$ is a unit for 'Temperature Per Magnetic Flux Density' expressed as $K
    T^{-1}$.

units.label: Kelvin per Watt
units.description: Thermal resistance is a heat property and a measure of a temperature difference by which an object or material resists a heat flow (heat per time unit or thermal resistance). Thermal resistance is the reciprocal thermal conductance. Absolute thermal resistance is the temperature difference across a structure when a unit of heat energy flows through it in unit time. It is the reciprocal of thermal conductance. The SI units of thermal resistance are kelvins per watt or the equivalent degrees Celsius per watt (the two are the same since as intervals).

units.label: Katal
units.description:
A unit of catalytic activity used especially in the chemistry of enzymes. A catalyst is a substance that
    starts or speeds a chemical reaction. Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts within the bodies of living plants and
    animals. A catalyst has an activity of one katal if it enables a reaction to proceed at the rate of one mole per second.

units.label: Katal per Litre
units.description:
A unit of catalytic activity used especially in the chemistry of enzymes. A catalyst is a substance
    that starts or speeds a chemical reaction. Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts within the bodies of living plants and
    animals. A catalyst has an activity of one katal if it enables a reaction to proceed at the rate of one mole per second.

units.label: Katal per Cubic Metre
units.description: the SI derived unit katal divided by the SI base unit metre to the power three

units.label: Katal per Microlitre
units.description:
A unit of catalytic activity used especially in the chemistry of enzymes. A catalyst is a substance
    that starts or speeds a chemical reaction. Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts within the bodies of living plants and
    animals. A catalyst has an activity of one katal if it enables a reaction to proceed at the rate of one mole per second.

units.label: Kip
units.description: 1000 pound-force

units.label: Kip per Square Inch
units.description: "Kip per Square Inch" is a unit for  'Force Per Area' expressed as $kip/in^{2}$.

units.label: Knot
units.description:
The knot (pronounced 'not') is a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile (1.852 km) per hour,
    approximately 1.151 mph. The abbreviation $kn$ is preferred by the International Hydrographic Organization (IHO), which
    includes every major sea-faring nation; however, the abbreviations kt (singular) and kts (plural) are also widely used.
    However, use of the abbreviation kt for knot conflicts with the SI symbol for kilotonne. The knot is a non-SI unit accepted
    for use with the International System of Units (SI). Worldwide, the knot is used in meteorology, and in maritime and air
    navigation - for example, a vessel travelling at 1 knot along a meridian travels one minute of geographic latitude in one
    hour. Etymologically, the term knot derives from counting the number of knots in the line that unspooled from the reel of a
    chip log in a specific time.

units.label: Knot per Second
units.description: $\textit{Knot per Second}$ is a unit for 'Linear Acceleration' expressed as $kt/s$.

units.label: Kibibit
units.description: 1,024-fold of the unit bit

units.label: Kibibit per Metre
units.description: 1024-fold of the unit bit divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Kibibit per Square Metre
units.description: 1024-fold of the unit bit divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 2

units.label: Kibibit per Cubic Metre
units.description: 1024-fold of the unit bit divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the exponent 3

units.label: Kibibyte
units.description: The kibibyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information equivalent to 1024 bytes.

units.label: Kiloampere Hour
units.description: product of the 1 000-fold of the SI base unit ampere and the unit hour

units.label: Kiloampere per Kelvin
units.description: 1,000-fold of the SI base unit ampere divided by the SI base unit kelvin

units.label: Kiloampere per Metre
units.description: 1 000-fold of the SI base unit ampere divided by the SI base unit metre

units.label: Kiloampere per Square Metre
units.description:
1 000-fold of the SI base unit ampere divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 2

units.label: Kilobar
units.description:
The bar is a non-SI unit of pressure, defined by the IUPAC as exactly equal to 100,000 Pa. It is about
    equal to the atmospheric pressure on Earth at sea level, and since 1982 the IUPAC has recommended that the standard for
    atmospheric pressure should be harmonized to $100,000 Pa = 1 bar \approx 750.0616827 Torr$. Units derived from the bar are
    the megabar (symbol: Mbar), kilobar (symbol: kbar), decibar (symbol: dbar), centibar (symbol: cbar), and millibar (symbol:
    mbar or mb). They are not SI or cgs units, but they are accepted for use with the SI.

units.label: Kilobaud
units.description: 1,000-fold of the unit baud for the symbol rate in communications engineering and telecommunication

units.label: Kilobit
units.description: 1,000-fold of the unit bit

units.label: Kilobit per Second
units.description: A kilobit per second (kB/s) is a unit of data transfer rate equal to 1,000 bits per second.

units.label: Kilobecquerel
units.description: 1 000-fold of the SI derived unit becquerel

units.label: Kilobecquerel per Kilogram
units.description: 1,000-fold of the SI derived unit becquerel divided by the SI base unit kilogram

units.label: Kilo British Thermal Unit (international Definition) per Square Foot
units.description: kBTU per Square Foot is an Imperial unit for 'Energy Per Area.

units.label: Kilo British Thermal Unit (international Definition) per Hour
Kilo British Thermal Unit (thermochemical Definition) per Hour
units.description: unit of the heat energy according to the Imperial system of units divided by the unit hour

units.label: Kilobyte
units.description:
The kilobyte is a multiple of the unit byte for digital information equivalent to 1000 bytes. Although
    the prefix kilo- means 1000, the term kilobyte and symbol kB have historically been used to refer to either 1024 (210) bytes
    or 1000 (103) bytes, dependent upon context, in the fields of computer science and information technology. This ambiguity is
    removed in QUDT, with KibiBYTE used to refer to 1024 bytes.

units.label: Kilobyte per Second
units.description:
A kilobyte per second (kByte/s) is a unit of data transfer rate equal to 1000 bytes per second or 8000
    bits per second.

units.label: Kilocoulomb per Square Metre
units.description:
1 000-fold of the SI derived unit coulomb divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 2

units.label: Kilocoulomb per Cubic Metre
units.description:
1 000-fold of the SI derived unit coulomb divided by the power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3

units.label: Kilocalorie
units.description: A $\textit{Kilocalorie}$ is a unit for $\textit{Energy And Work}$ expressed as $kcal$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Centimetre Second Degree Celsius
Kilocalorie per Square Centimetre
units.description: "Kilocalorie per Square Centimeter" is a unit for  'Energy Per Area' expressed as $kcal/cm^{2}$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Square Centimetre Minute
units.description:
"Kilocalorie per Square Centimeter Minute" is a unit for  'Power Per Area' expressed as
    $kcal/(cm^{2}-min)$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Square Centimetre Second
units.description:
"Kilocalorie per Square Centimeter Second" is a unit for  'Power Per Area' expressed as
    $kcal/(cm^{2}-s)$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Gram
units.description: "Kilocalorie per Gram" is a unit for  'Specific Energy' expressed as $kcal/gm$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Gram Degree Celsius
units.description:
$\textit{Calorie per Gram Degree Celsius}$ is a unit for 'Specific Heat Capacity' expressed as
    $kcal/(gm-degC)$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Minute
units.description:
A $\textit{Kilocalorie per Minute}$ is a unit for $\textit{Heat Flow Rate}$ and $\textit{Power}$,
   expressed as $kcal/min$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Mole
units.description:
The kilocalorie per mole is a derived unit of energy per Avogadro's number of particles. It is the quotient of a kilocalorie (1000 thermochemical gram calories) and a mole, mainly used in the United States. In SI units, it is equal to $4.184 kJ/mol$, or $6.9477 \times 10 J per molecule$. At room temperature it is equal to 1.688 . Physical quantities measured in $kcal\cdot mol$ are usually thermodynamical quantities; mostly free energies such as: Heat of vaporization Heat of fusion

.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Mole Degree Celsius
units.description:
A $\textit{Kilocalorie per Mole Degree Celsius}$ is a unit for 'Molar Heat Capacity',
   expressed as $kcal/(mol-degC)$.

units.label: Kilocalorie per Second
units.description:
A $\textit{Kilocalorie per Second}$ is a unit for $\textit{Heat Flow Rate}$ and $\textit{Power}$,
   expressed as $kcal/s$.

units.label: Kilo International Table Calorie
units.description: 1000-fold of the unit calorie, which is used particularly for calorific values of food

units.label: Kilo International Table Calorie per Gram Kelvin
units.description:
unit of the mass-related heat capacity as quotient 1,000-fold of the calorie (international table)
    divided by the product of the 0.001-fold of the SI base units kilogram and kelvin

units.label: Kilo International Table Calorie per Hour Metre Degree Celsius
units.description:
1 000-fold of the no longer approved unit international calorie for energy divided by the product
    of the SI base unit metre, the unit hour for time and the unit degree Celsius for temperature

units.label: Kilocalorie (Mean)
units.description: 1000-fold of the unit calorie, which is used particularly for calorific values of food

units.label: Kilo Thermochemical Calorie
units.description: 1000-fold of the unit calorie, which is used particularly for calorific values of food

units.label: Kilo Thermochemical Calorie per Hour
units.description: 1 000-fold of the non-legal unit thermochemical calorie divided by the unit hour

units.label: Kilo Thermochemical Calorie per Minute
units.description: 1000-fold of the unit calorie divided by the unit minute

units.label: Kilo Thermochemical Calorie per Second
units.description: 1000-fold of the unit calorie divided by the SI base unit second

units.label: Kilocandela
units.description: 1,000-fold of the SI base unit candela

units.label: Kilocurie
units.description: 1 000-fold of the unit curie

units.label: Kilocurie
units.description: 1 000-fold of the unit curie

units.label: Kilo Cubic Foot
units.description: 1 000-fold of the unit cubic foot.

units.label: Kilo Electron Volt
units.description: "Kilo Electron Volt" is a unit for  'Energy And Work' expressed as $keV$.

units.label: Kilo Electron Volt per Micrometre
units.description: "Kilo Electron Volt per Micrometer" is a unit for  'Linear Energy Transfer' expressed as $keV/microM$.

units.label: Kilofarad
units.description: 1,000-fold of the SI derived unit farad

units.label: Kilogauss
units.description: 1 000-fold of the CGS unit of the magnetic flux density B

units.label: Kilogram
units.description:
The kilogram or kilogramme (SI symbol: kg), also known as the kilo, is the base unit of mass in the
    International System of Units and is defined as being equal to the mass of the International Prototype Kilogram (IPK), which
    is almost exactly equal to the mass of one liter of water. The avoirdupois (or international) pound, used in both the Imperial
    system and U.S. customary units, is defined as exactly 0.45359237 kg, making one kilogram approximately equal to 2.2046
    avoirdupois pounds.

units.label: Kilogram Centimetre per Second
units.description:
product of the SI base unit kilogram and the 0.01-fold of the SI base unit metre divided by the SI base
    unit second

units.label: Kilogram Square Centimetre
units.description:
product of the SI base unit kilogram and the 0 0001fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with
    the exponent 2

units.label: Kilogram Kelvin
units.description: $\textit{Kilogram Kelvin}$ is a unit for 'Mass Temperature' expressed as $kg-K$.

units.label: Kilogram Metre
units.description: unit of the imbalance as a product of the SI base unit kilogram and the SI base unit metre

units.label: Kilogram Metre per Second
units.description: "Kilogram Meter Per Second" is a unit for  'Linear Momentum' expressed as $kg-m/s$.

units.label: Kilogram Metre per Square Second
units.description:
product of the SI base unit kilogram and the SI base unit metre divided by the power of the SI base unit
    second by exponent 2

units.label: Kilogram Square Metre
units.description: "Kilogram Square Meter" is a unit for  'Moment Of Inertia' expressed as $kg-m^2$.

units.label: Kilogram Square Metre per Second
units.description: "Kilogram Square Meter Per Second" is a unit for  'Angular Momentum' expressed as $kg-m^2-s^{-1}$.

units.label: Kilogram Square Millimetre
units.description:
product of the SI base kilogram and the  0.001-fold of the power of the SI base metre with the
    exponent 2

units.label: Kilogram per Bar
units.description: SI base unit kilogram divided by the unit bar

units.label: Kilogram per Square Centimetre
units.description:
SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.0001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre by exponent
    2

units.label: Kilogram per Cubic Centimetre
units.description:
SI base unit kilogram divided by the 0.000 001-fold of the power of the SI base unit metre with the
    exponent 3

units.label: Kilogram per Cubic Centimetre Bar
units.description:
SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.000001-fold of the power of the SI base unit
    metre with the exponent 3 and the unit bar

units.label: Kilogram per Cubic Centimetre Kelvin
units.description:
SI base unit kilogram divided by the product out of the 0.000001-fold of the power of the SI base unit
    metre with the exponent 3 and the SI base unit

units.label: Kilogram per Day
units.description: SI base unit kilogram divided by the unit day

units.label: Kilogram per Day Bar

units.label: Pound Mass per Hour
units.description:
Pound per hour is a mass flow unit. It is abbreviated as PPH or more conventionally as lb/h. Fuel flow
    for engines is usually expressed using this unit, it is particularly useful when dealing with gases or liquids as volume flow
    varies more with temperature and pressure. $1 lb/h = 0.4535927 kg/h = 126.00 mg/s$.  Minimum fuel intake on a jumbojet can be
    as low as 150 lb/h when idling, however this is not enough to sustain flight.
